neet_che_u19_t02_1.working: Prolonged heating with HI reduces all the -OH groups and the carbonyl group of glucose. This leaves the unbranched C6 chain as n-hexane, which shows the six carbons are in a straight chain.

neet_che_u19_t02_2.working: Nitric acid oxidises both the -CHO group and the terminal -CH2OH group to -COOH, giving saccharic (glucaric) acid. Formation of this dicarboxylic acid shows a primary alcohol group is present. Bromine water oxidises only the -CHO group.

neet_che_u19_t02_3.working: An open-chain aldehyde should form a bisulphite adduct with NaHSO3. Glucose does not, which only the cyclic hemiacetal structure explains. The other three facts are consistent with the open-chain structure.

neet_che_u19_t02_4.working: Fructose is a reducing sugar: in alkaline Tollens' medium it isomerises through an enediol and has a free hemiketal, so A is true. R is false because ketoses such as fructose are also reducing sugars.

neet_che_u19_t02_5.working: Statement I is correct: alpha- and beta-D-glucose are anomers differing only at C1, and the NCERT melting points are 419 K and 423 K. Statement II is correct: fructose's C5 -OH attacks C2 to form a five-membered furanose ring, while glucose forms a six-membered pyranose ring.
